en.title: Street Fighter Knocks Out Box Office; Elizabeth Holmes Doc Rises
en.summary: The legendary fighting game franchise makes a powerful return to the silver screen, dominating the weekend box office. Meanwhile, a documentary diving into the controversial life of Elizabeth Holmes is also drawing significant attention.
en.body:
The roar of the crowd and the crunch of digital combat have translated into box office gold this weekend, as **Street Fighter** lands a knockout blow with an estimated $31 million in its opening frame. Paramount Pictures’ latest foray into the iconic fighting game franchise has clearly resonated with audiences, proving that the allure of high-octane action and familiar characters remains a potent draw.

The film, which generated a strong $13 million on Friday alone, has outperformed expectations and secured the top spot in a competitive weekend. This success marks a significant win for the **Street Fighter** IP, which has a long history of theatrical releases, though not always with the same level of critical or commercial fanfare. The film’s performance suggests a renewed appetite for game-to-screen adaptations that can capture the spirit of their source material.

## The Rise of Real-Life Drama

While **Street Fighter** took the top prize, the weekend also saw a compelling performance from the Elizabeth Holmes documentary, **You Can See Everything**. This A24 release has been making waves, drawing significant crowds and demonstrating the enduring public fascination with the Theranos founder’s dramatic rise and fall. The documentary’s strong showing indicates that audiences are hungry for compelling non-fiction narratives that explore ambition, deception, and the consequences of unchecked power.

This pairing of a blockbuster video game adaptation and a gripping true-crime documentary highlights the diverse tastes of today's moviegoers. Audiences are clearly seeking both escapism and introspection at the cinema, with both genres finding their champions this weekend.

## Sinking Hopes and New Beginnings

In stark contrast to the weekend’s winners, the survival thriller **Whalefall** struggled to make a significant impact. Debuting with an estimated $3 million on Friday, the film is projected to bring in only $7 million by Sunday. This performance suggests that the film, despite its intriguing premise, failed to capture the audience’s imagination or compete with the broader appeal of **Street Fighter** and **You Can See Everything**.

The weekend also saw the debut of **Sense and Sensibility**, though details on its box office performance were not as readily available. The presence of these varied films on the marquee underscores the dynamic nature of the box office, where established franchises, compelling documentaries, and genre thrillers all vie for attention.

What's Next

With **Street Fighter** leading the charge, all eyes will be on its second-weekend performance to see if it can maintain its momentum. Meanwhile, the strong reception for **You Can See Everything** suggests it will be a significant contender in the documentary space for weeks to come. Audiences looking for a different kind of cinematic experience will undoubtedly be following these stories closely.

content_raw: A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary is causing quite a stir over the weekend as 'Sense and Sensibility' also debuts.
